title: 1 Kings 8
paragraphs: ¹ Then Solomon summoned the elders of Israel, the heads of the tribes, and the leaders of the ancestral families — all the chiefs of the Israelites — to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the City of David, which is Zion. ² They all gathered around King Solomon at the festival in the seventh month, the month of Ethanim. ³ When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the priests lifted the ark ⁴ and carried it up, along with the tent of meeting and all the sacred vessels that were in it. The priests and Levites carried everything up together. ⁵ King Solomon and the entire assembly of Israel were gathered before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and cattle that they could not be counted.

⁶ The priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD into the inner sanctuary — the Most Holy Place — and set it beneath the wings of the cherubim. ⁷ The cherubim spread their wings over the ark, sheltering it and its poles from above. ⁸ The poles extended outward and their ends could be seen from the Holy Place just in front of the inner sanctuary, though they could not be seen from outside. They are still there to this day. ⁹ There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed there at Horeb, where the LORD made his covenant with Israel after bringing them out of Egypt. ¹⁰ When the priests withdrew from the Holy Place, the cloud filled the house of the LORD —

¹¹ so thick that the priests could not continue to minister, because the glory of the LORD had filled his house. ¹² Then Solomon spoke: "The LORD has said that he would dwell in thick darkness. ¹³ I have indeed built you a magnificent house, a place for you to live forever." ¹⁴ Then the king turned to face the congregation of Israel, who were all standing there, and he blessed them. ¹⁵ "Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel," he said, "who with his own mouth made a promise to my father David and with his own hand has fulfilled it."

¹⁶ "From the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city from any of the tribes of Israel in which to build a house where my name would be — but I chose David to rule over my people Israel. ¹⁷ It was in my father David's heart to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel. ¹⁸ But the LORD said to David, 'You had the intention — and it was good that you had it. ¹⁹ Nevertheless, it is not you who will build the house; it is your son, born of your own body, who will build the house for my name.' ²⁰ The LORD has kept the promise he made. I have succeeded my father David and now sit on the throne of Israel, just as the LORD promised. And I have built this house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel."

²¹ "I have also provided a place there for the ark, which holds the covenant the LORD made with our ancestors when he brought them out of Egypt." ²² Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands toward heaven. ²³ He prayed: "LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven above or on earth below — you who keep your covenant of love with your servants who walk faithfully before you with all their heart. ²⁴ You have kept your promise to your servant, my father David. You spoke it with your own mouth and fulfilled it with your own hand, as it is today. ²⁵ Now LORD, God of Israel, keep for my father David the promise you made to him: 'You will never fail to have a successor sitting before me on the throne of Israel, if only your descendants walk faithfully in my ways as you have walked.'"

²⁶ "Now, God of Israel, let your word — the word you spoke to your servant David my father — be confirmed. ²⁷ But will God really live on earth? Even the heavens, the highest heavens, cannot contain you — how much less this house I have built! ²⁸ Even so, hear the prayer of your servant and his plea for mercy, LORD my God. Listen to the cry and the prayer that your servant is praying before you today. ²⁹ May your eyes be open toward this house night and day, toward the place of which you said, 'My name shall be there,' so that you will hear the prayer your servant prays toward this place. ³⁰ Hear the prayer of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from heaven, your dwelling place, and when you hear — forgive."

³¹ "When someone wrongs their neighbor and is required to take an oath, and they come to swear before your altar in this house — ³² then hear from heaven and act. Judge between your servants: declare the guilty person guilty and bring their actions back on their own head, and declare the innocent person innocent. ³³ When your people Israel are defeated before their enemies because they have sinned against you, and when they turn back to you and acknowledge your name and pray and plead with you in this house — ³⁴ then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land you gave their ancestors. ³⁵ When the sky is shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, and when they pray toward this place and confess your name and turn from their sin because you have disciplined them —"

³⁶ "— then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your servants and your people Israel. Teach them the right way to live, and send rain on the land you gave them as an inheritance. ³⁷ When there is famine or plague in the land — drought, blight, locusts, or grasshoppers — or when enemies besiege their towns, or when any disaster or sickness strikes — ³⁸ then when any of your people Israel pray and spread out their hands toward this house, each one aware of their own affliction and suffering — ³⁹ hear from heaven, your dwelling place. Forgive them, and deal with each according to their deeds, for you know their hearts — you alone know every human heart. ⁴⁰ So they will stand in reverence before you all the days of their lives in the land you gave our ancestors."

⁴¹ "As for the foreigner who does not belong to your people Israel but has come from a distant land because of your name — ⁴² for they will hear of your great name and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm — when they come and pray toward this house, ⁴³ then hear from heaven, your dwelling place, and grant whatever they ask. Do this so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as your own people Israel do — and so that they may know that this house I have built bears your name. ⁴⁴ When your people go out to battle against their enemies, wherever you send them, and they pray to the LORD toward this city you have chosen and toward this house I have built for your name — ⁴⁵ then hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause."

⁴⁶ "When they sin against you — for there is no one who does not sin — and you grow angry with them and give them over to their enemies, who carry them off as captives to a land far or near; ⁴⁷ yet if they come to their senses in the land of their captivity and repent and plead with you there, saying, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly'; ⁴⁸ and if they turn back to you with all their heart and soul in the land of their enemies who captured them, and pray to you toward their land — the land you gave their ancestors — toward this city you have chosen and toward this house I have built for your name: ⁴⁹ then hear from heaven, your dwelling place, their prayer and their plea. Uphold their cause. ⁵⁰ Forgive your people who have sinned against you and all the offenses they have committed against you. Move their captors to show them compassion —"

⁵¹ "— for they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out of Egypt, out of that iron furnace. ⁵² May your eyes be open to the plea of your servant and to the plea of your people Israel, and may you hear them whenever they cry out to you. ⁵³ For you singled them out from all the peoples of the earth to be your own inheritance — just as you declared through your servant Moses when you brought our ancestors out of Egypt, LORD God." ⁵⁴ When Solomon finished making this entire prayer and plea to the LORD, he rose from before the altar, where he had been kneeling with his hands stretched out toward heaven. ⁵⁵ He stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel in a loud voice:

⁵⁶ "Praise be to the LORD, who has given rest to his people Israel, just as he promised. Not one word has failed of all the good promises he gave through his servant Moses. ⁵⁷ May the LORD our God be with us, as he was with our ancestors. May he never leave us or abandon us. ⁵⁸ May he turn our hearts toward him, to walk in all his ways and to keep the commands, decrees, and laws he gave our ancestors. ⁵⁹ And may these words I have prayed before the LORD be near to the LORD our God day and night, so that he upholds the cause of his servant and the cause of his people Israel according to each day's need — ⁶⁰ so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God and there is no other."

⁶¹ "And may your hearts be fully committed to the LORD our God, to walk in his decrees and obey his commands, as you are doing today." ⁶² Then the king and all Israel with him offered sacrifices before the LORD. ⁶³ Solomon offered as a fellowship offering to the LORD twenty-two thousand cattle and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep and goats. So the king and all the Israelites dedicated the house of the LORD. ⁶⁴ That same day the king consecrated the middle area of the courtyard in front of the LORD's house and offered there the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and the fat of the fellowship offerings, because the bronze altar before the LORD was too small to hold them all. ⁶⁵ Solomon held the festival at that time, and all Israel with him — a vast assembly stretching from the entrance of Hamath to the Wadi of Egypt — before the LORD our God, for fourteen days.

⁶⁶ On the fifteenth day he sent the people home. They blessed the king and left for their homes, joyful and glad, grateful for all the goodness the LORD had shown to his servant David and to his people Israel.
